title: sé, él, ella, tengo que, -pose → poner, cuándo

cards.title: sé = I know (irregular)
cards.body: Saber's I form is sé, not 'sabo'. It's short, so people often say lo sé (I know it). The other forms are regular.

cards.title: 'he' is inside the verb
cards.body: Quiere already includes 'he'. Lo means him (object), not he. Get used to two English words becoming one Spanish word.

examples.en: I don't know what he wants.

cards.title: él = he; ella = she
cards.body: Add él or ella for emphasis, to clarify, or to contrast. Ll sounds like 'y'. Emphasis is best learned live, through tone and gesture.

examples.en: I don't know what HE wants.
examples.es: No sé qué él quiere. / No sé qué quiere él.

examples.en: I don't want to invite him, but she does.
examples.es: (Yo) no quiero invitarlo, pero ella sí.

cards.title: salir: only the I form is irregular
cards.body: Check the verb type first (salir: -ir) to avoid 'sele'. Salir is a movement verb, so it takes a before another verb.

cards.title: tengo que = I have to
cards.body: Tengo = I have; add que and it means 'I have to'. Que (also 'that' / 'what') has no neat translation here.

examples.es: Tengo que hacerlo. / Lo tengo que hacer.

cards.title: tiene, viene — the g only in the I form
cards.body: Tener: tengo, tiene, tienen, tienes. Venir: vengo, viene, vienen, vienes.

cards.title: cuándo = when
cards.body: Don't let English 'are you coming' confuse you: just when + you come.

examples.en: When are you coming to eat?
I want to know what she has.

cards.title: Irregularities spread to related verbs
cards.body: Tengo → obtengo. Obtener is often used like 'get'.

cards.title: poner = to put; -pose → -poner
cards.body: I put = pongo. English -pose verbs become -poner and share its irregularity. Supongo que sí = I suppose so.

cards.title: tengo que vs debo
cards.body: Like English: debo (must) is more serious; tengo que (have to) is everyday.

cards.title: Verbs + 'to' form
cards.body: Put a 'to' form straight after these: voy a, puedo (think 'power'), tengo que, debo, quiero.

examples.en: I'm going to try to eat later.
examples.es: Voy a intentar comer más tarde.

practice.en: I don't know what he wants.
I don't want to invite him, but she does.
es: No quiero invitarlo pero ella sí
Yo no quiero invitarlo pero ella sí

practice.why: Only the I form is irregular: salen.
debo = must (more serious than tengo que).
